final_answer: When an mRNA vaccine is injected, it enters muscle cells near the injection site. The mRNA carries instructions for making a harmless piece of the virus protein (like the spike protein). The cell uses this mRNA to produce the protein, which is displayed on its surface. Immune cells recognize the protein as foreign and activate B and T cells. B cells produce antibodies to neutralize the virus, while T cells destroy infected cells. Memory cells remain to provide long-term immunity if the real virus is encountered. This process is safe.
